record.title: Nakonde–Tunduma COVID closure followed by limited cargo reopening in May 2020
record.scope: Nakonde–Tunduma crossing and associated Nakonde movement restriction; measured endpoint is initial cargo restoration only.
record.crossings: Nakonde / Tunduma One Stop Border Post
record.direction: Both freight directions reopened, initially trucks destined for Tanzania.
record.movement: Cross-border cargo and ordinary people initially affected; cargo resumed while ordinary passenger crossing remained prohibited.
record.exceptions: Reopening prioritised cargo, including essential fuel, food and medical supplies. Passenger reopening not established by the cargo evidence.
record.imposing_authority: Zambian presidency and health authorities; Zambia Revenue Authority administered border operations.
record.enforcement: Border closure implemented by Zambian authorities; operational interviews describe truck movement resuming.
record.consequences: Interrupted export/import truck flow; volume of losses not quantified here.
record.relationship: No matching Nakonde closure found in all 528 audited baseline records. Distinct frontier from Zambia–DRC SC03 and the Tanzanian restrictions on Kenyan truckers.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no inference of status at the 2026-10-21 cutoff.
record.official_rationale: Contain the Nakonde COVID outbreak through screening, health-worker retraining and targeted interventions.
record.context: Officials reported an outbreak concentrated in the border town; the closure interrupted a regional mining and essential-supplies corridor.
record.uncertainty: Official and same-day sources specify May 11 effective closure; Reuters retrospectively says Sunday May 10 and five days. May 15 actual trucks are secure, but the onset discrepancy prevents exact duration. Later May 22/23 business/notices are not substituted for first cargo passage.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. Bounded closure and cargo restart are documented, but May 10/11 onset wording conflicts. No precise numeric interval; ordinary passengers remained restricted after May 15.
